newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Ireland's Robinson is leading UN rights candidate.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Robinson is leading UN rights candidate.

text.p: Sonia Picado, Costa Rica's ambassador to the United States, has indicated she would not be chosen as U.N. human rights commissioner, thereby leaving Irish President Mary Robinson as the clear favorite.
Picado, who met U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Thursday, said she had been offered alternative jobs related to human rights.
It was her second visit with him, the first one being on April 3. Robinson was in New York last Friday and spoke to Annan but revealed little of substance about their talks.
The two women were the leading candidates for the post of U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights, based in Geneva.

Picado, in answer to questions, said Annan had not offered her the job at their Thursday meeting. "My highest option would be high commissioner but there are other options the secretary-general also wants me to study," she said.
Annan is not expected to announce his decision until July.

The position, first proposed nearly 50 years ago, became vacant after Jose Ayala Lasso resigned in March as the first U.N. human rights commissioner to become Ecuador's foreign minister. He was appointed in 1994 for four years.
In the interim, the job is being carried out by Briton Ralph Zacklin, a deputy to the U.N. under-secretary general for legal affairs.

An author and former judge and law school dean, Picado is backed by most Latin American states. Robinson is supported by the United States and Britain and several human rights groups as well as her own government.
The appointment has to be approved by the General Assembly, which is dominated by developing countries.
Robinson, also a lawyer and human rights expert, does not end her seven-year term as president until December although there are reports she would be available in November.
Annan had considerd a deputy high commissioner post, diplomats said, and human rights groups want him to appoint a rights coordinator in New York.
Picado said she did not want to be a deputy, explaining: If I am not the high commissioner, I am not sure that I want to accept another post." Friday, 30 May 1997 05:46:07 ENDS nN2950936
